subject: Dedicated pool failover sequence and customer mitigation plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Diane Talbot <diane.talbot@acme-corp.com>, support@acme-corp.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:04:15 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool failover sequence and customer mitigation plan

Diane —

Quick update from our side: between 08:55–09:20 PT this morning one of the reserved GPU pools serving Acme experienced a failover sequence that led to request queuing and elevated latency for a subset of your production queries (we estimate ~12 minutes of degraded throughput for heavy-batch jobs). Impact was isolated to your dedicated cluster nodes in us-west-2; hosted endpoints and other regions were unaffected.

What we did immediately
- Redirected new allocations to the warm-standby pool and increased ephemeral burst capacity for Acme traffic.
- Enabled a temporary throttling policy on long-running generator requests to reduce head-of-line blocking.
- Applied a hotfix to the allocator service to stop the repeated reallocation loop.

Attached: a short timeline CSV (acme_incident_timeline.csv) and an initial postmortem draft (postmortem-draft.pdf). I know you’ll want details — Karthik and Monica are on this thread and will add the technical root cause and next steps.

We’re proposing a 2% credit for the affected billing window and would like to set a technical call today at 16:00 PT to walk through the root cause and our remediation milestones. Please let me know if that time works or propose an alternate.

Appreciate your patience — we’ll get this fully resolved.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Diane Talbot <diane.talbot@acme-corp.com>, support@acme-corp.com

Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 10:12:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool failover sequence and customer mitigation plan

Hi all — adding the technical summary and immediate mitigations we executed.

Short RCA (initial)
- Root cause: an allocator race in the dedicated pool controller where parallel scale-in + rebalancing decisions could attempt to evict nodes that still had in-flight KV cache references. Under a burst of allocations (spike from a customer batch job), the allocator entered a reallocation loop that triggered eviction/thaw cycles for a subset of nodes. That caused queue buildup while nodes repeatedly reconstructed cache state.
- Trigger: a rare combination of long-tail token sequences from an Acme batch+concurrency spike and a timing window in the allocator code (we’ve reproduced locally and with a canary workload).

What we rolled out (timeline in attachments)
- 09:01 PT: Detect rule fired; we halted the allocator’s aggressive rebalancing path and forced allocations to warm-standby nodes.
- 09:07 PT: Temporary throttling and admission control for long-running generation requests to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- 09:14 PT: Hotfix deployed to allocator to prevent repeated eviction attempts; this ended the reallocation loop.
- 09:30 PT: Gradual lift of throttling after verifying steady-state.

Short-term follow-ups (next 48–72h)
- Enable stronger KV cache affinity heuristics for dedicated pools to reduce the chance of replays during failover.
- Add a guard that prevents the allocator from selecting a node for eviction if it has >X% active KV references.
- Increase warm-standby sizing for accounts with sustained burst patterns (Acme will have a modest bump for 72h while we validate).

Long-term remediation (2–3 weeks)
- Scheduler fix with formal correctness tests to prevent the race; extended canary across warm/warm-standby pools.
- Prometheus alerting for repeated eviction loops and a dashboard that surfaces this specific signal.

I’ve attached the draft postmortem; the final RCA will include logs and a replay artefact.

If the team on the call wants deeper traces, I’ll bring the allocator timeline and the repro script.

Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Diane — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the call. A few confirmations from our side:

- Warm-standby routing: we will keep the warm-standby route and increased sizing in place for the next 72 hours while we run canary traffic (this is already configured for your account and will not require any change on your end).
- Credit: we will apply a 2% service credit to the affected billing period; the credit will appear as an invoice line item on your next monthly invoice. I’ll follow up with billing confirmation after this thread.
- Likelihood of recurrence: after the hotfix and the added guard rails we estimate recurrence probability for this specific race condition to be <1% for similar workloads; until the full scheduler fix is in production we’re conservatively treating it as a low-probability, non-zero risk. Karthik will run an extended canary for 48 hours and share the test results.

Related references for the call:
- Support ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-9421
- Draft postmortem: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcPostMortem

Next steps for the call (agenda)
1) Walkthrough of the reproduced race (Karthik) — 15 minutes
2) Mitigation steps we’ve applied and monitoring plan (Monica) — 10 minutes
3) Q&A and follow-up actions & credits (Jordan) — 10 minutes

Monica will share the short runbook we’ll hand you for cross-ops coordination (how to adjust batch windows or transient throttle settings if needed). Thanks again — we’ll be on the call at 16:00 PT.

Best,
Jordan Blake
